characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements for every material state
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching gave a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace and were successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast, the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
After cooling and cutting, the 10 × 50 × 130 mm³-sized blocks were obtained.
Hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
This is the defining heat treatment of this sample: aged in air at 450 °C for 24 h, then oil quenched.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm with some retained microsegregations of Mn

unmapped_findings: For the intermediate Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al alloy, the paper states that alloys with Al additions of 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening). [b0024]

In the RAP screening, the intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al do not show equivalent mechanical properties to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior is observed in the 2–6 wt.% Al cases. [b0025]

In Fig. 4 (tensile strength vs elongation), the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al (dark navy) data points lie between ~670–770 MPa tensile strength and ~30–55% elongation; this cluster aggregates multiple aging conditions (450/500/550/600 °C, 1 h and 24 h) and is not specific to the 450 °C/24 h condition. [figure_004][b0029]

In Fig. 3, hardness is nearly flat at ~200 HBW from 0 to 6 wt.% Al before rising steeply toward ~375 HBW at 8 wt.% Al; the legend annotates 450 °C/1 h but not the 450 °C/24 h condition, so no specific YS/UTS/TE/hardness values for the 450 °C/24 h, 6Al sample are individually reported. [figure_003][b0028]

The nominal composition of this sample is Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al (wt.%), i.e., 30 wt.% Mn, 1.2 wt.% C, 6 wt.% Al, balance Fe; it belongs to the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl (x = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 wt.% Al) RAP matrix. [b0019][b0024]

From Fig. 1, Fe-Mn-Al-C steels near ~6 wt.% Al correspond to a mass density around 7.15 g/cm³ (approximate reading from the descending teal-square series that starts at ~6 wt.% Al); this is an alloy-level density estimate, not specific to the 450 °C/24 h aging condition. [figure_001]
